issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the solution use a Stock.emptyStock() method, but the template's Stock class defines clearInventory() instead. This naming mismatch can cause students to follow the UML and call emptyStock() (or implement code expecting emptyStock()), which will not compile against the provided template. It creates a blocking inconsistency between the UML/specification and the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either rename the template's clearInventory() method to emptyStock(), or add an emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory(). Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to refer to clearInventory() instead of emptyStock(), so all three artifacts use the same identifier.
